skill.name: stripe-best-practices
skill.description: Guides Stripe integration decisions — API selection (Checkout Sessions vs PaymentIntents), Connect platform setup (Accounts v2, controller properties), billing/subscriptions, Treasury financial accounts, integration surfaces (Checkout, Payment Element), migrating from deprecated Stripe APIs, and security best practices (API key management, restricted keys, webhooks, OAuth). Use when building, modifying, or reviewing any Stripe integration — including accepting payments, building marketplaces, integrating Stripe, processing payments, setting up subscriptions, creating connected accounts, or implementing secure key handling.

content.value_statement: Stripe integrations involve many API choices, security rules, and deprecated patterns. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code toward current Stripe implementation practices.
actual_capabilities: Routes payment, billing, Connect, Tax, Treasury, and security questions to focused reference guidance.
Recommends current Stripe APIs, including Checkout Sessions, PaymentIntents, SetupIntents, Accounts v2, and v2 Financial Accounts.
Identifies deprecated Stripe patterns such as Charges API, Sources API, Card Element, and legacy Connect account types.
Explains secure key handling with restricted API keys, vault storage, rotation, IP allowlists, and pre-commit checks.
Guides webhook signature verification, OAuth state validation, and safer Dashboard access controls.
limitations: It does not replace Stripe documentation, legal advice, tax advice, or compliance review.
It cannot verify a live Stripe account, Dashboard setting, webhook endpoint, or API key permission.
It may need current Stripe documentation when API behavior changes after the bundled references were written.
It provides implementation guidance, not automated code execution or account configuration.

use_cases.title: Plan a New Checkout Flow
use_cases.description: A developer chooses Checkout, Payment Element, or PaymentIntents while avoiding deprecated APIs and card-only assumptions.

use_cases.title: Review a Marketplace Integration
use_cases.description: A platform team checks Connect account setup, charge type selection, liability choices, and onboarding approach before launch.

use_cases.title: Harden Stripe Security Controls
use_cases.description: A security reviewer evaluates API key handling, webhook verification, OAuth state checks, and Dashboard access safeguards.

prompt_templates.title: Choose the Right Stripe API
prompt_templates.prompt: I am building [one-time payment, subscription, marketplace, or saved payment method]. Use this skill to recommend the Stripe API and explain why.

prompt_templates.title: Review an Existing Integration
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Stripe implementation plan for deprecated APIs, payment method configuration mistakes, and missing security controls: [paste plan].

prompt_templates.title: Design a Connect Platform
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Connect integration for [marketplace model]. Cover Accounts v2, controller responsibilities, charge type, onboarding, and security risks.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Migration Checklist
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a migration checklist from [current Stripe pattern] to current Stripe guidance. Include API changes, security changes, rollout steps, and tests.

output_examples.input: Which Stripe API should I use for a new subscription checkout?
output_examples.output: The skill recommends Billing APIs with Checkout Sessions. It explains initial payment handling, trials, proration, and customer portal management.

output_examples.input: Review my marketplace setup before launch.
output_examples.output: The skill checks Accounts v2 usage, controller responsibilities, charge type selection, onboarding approach, and Connect liability concerns.

output_examples.input: A Stripe key may have been exposed in source control.
output_examples.output: The skill prioritizes rolling the key, reviewing request activity, moving secrets to a vault, and adding key leak prevention checks.

best_practices: Prefer Stripe-hosted or embedded Checkout for standard payment flows before building custom payment logic.
Use restricted API keys with least privilege, vault storage, rotation, and separate environments.
Verify webhook signatures and use OAuth state checks for every Connect authorization flow.
anti_patterns: Hardcoding Stripe secret keys in source code, mobile apps, client-side code, logs, or examples.
Using deprecated Charges, Sources, Card Element, or legacy Connect account type patterns for new integrations.
Manually restricting payment_method_types when dynamic payment methods or Dashboard configuration should decide eligible methods.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps choose and review Stripe integration patterns for payments, billing, Connect, Tax, Treasury, and security.

faq.question: Does it write complete production code?
faq.answer: It can guide implementation choices, but production code still needs testing, monitoring, and review against Stripe documentation.

faq.question: Can it choose between Checkout and PaymentIntents?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains when Checkout Sessions are preferred and when PaymentIntents or SetupIntents are more appropriate.

faq.question: Can it review Stripe security practices?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers key handling, restricted API keys, webhook signatures, OAuth state checks, and Dashboard access controls.

faq.question: Does it cover Connect marketplaces?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers Accounts v2, controller responsibilities, charge types, onboarding, capabilities, and liability tradeoffs.

faq.question: Should I still check Stripe documentation?
faq.answer: Yes. Stripe APIs can change, so current Stripe documentation should be checked before launch or migration.
